name.text: Shared: Interpret a large quantity in standard form

questiontext.text:
A regional education programme reports that \[ {@quantity@} \] exercise books were distributed.

Write this quantity in standard form.

Coefficient \(a\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

Exponent \(n\): [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

The report also states that this is about {@scale_label@} books.

Is that scale description correct? Enter 1 for yes and 0 for no.

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The quantity is \[ {@quantity@}. \]

In standard form, \[ {@coefficient_display@} \times 10^{@exponent@}. \]

Because the exponent is \[ {@exponent@}, \] the quantity is on the scale of {@correct_scale_label@}.

So the scale statement in the question is {@scale_truth_text@}.

number-sense

large-number-context-standard-form

application

contextual-standard-form

Learners convert a large contextual quantity to standard form and interpret the magnitude represented by its exponent.

Targets learners who perform the numerical conversion correctly but fail to interpret the magnitude in context.

Original STACK question. NUMBAS-10751 is used only as an interaction reference. The contextual interpretation and diagnostic structure are original. No source wording or mathematical content is copied.

None.

Curriculum alignment is maintained outside the question source.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your standard-form conversion may be correct, but check the magnitude interpretation carefully.

prtincorrect.text: Use the exponent to interpret the scale of the quantity.

falsefeedback.text: Your coefficient is correct. Recheck the exponent.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You converted the quantity and interpreted its magnitude consistently.

node.description: Checks an incorrect interpretation of the contextual magnitude.

truefeedback.text:
Your standard-form conversion is correct, but the magnitude has been interpreted incorrectly.

Use the exponent to decide whether the quantity is in the hundreds of thousands, millions, or tens of millions.

falsefeedback.text: Recheck the magnitude represented by the exponent.

qtest.description: Correct conversion and magnitude interpretation receive full credit.
Correct standard-form conversion with incorrect magnitude interpretation receives partial credit.
